verdicts.evidence: a2a-runner.py reviewed in full (880 lines). TaskStore.finalize (lines 107-126) persists state+finished_at+artifact event+status event+events_complete atomically under one lock and is idempotent — a second finalize returns the existing record, so cancel/complete races yield exactly one terminal sequence. Executor process map is lock-guarded (_slots, lines 207-218); CancelTask sets cancel_requested, terminates the whole process group TERM->KILL (lines 402-432), and duplicate cancel returns the same terminal record. Graceful stop: SIGTERM/SIGINT -> request_shutdown -> shutdown_all cancels every ACTIVE task in parallel with bounded joins, force-terminates any slot whose cancel waiter timed out, then force-finalizes any still-ACTIVE record CANCELED (lines 434-467) — no infinite WORKING; HTTP server keeps serving GetTask/SSE through the drain window before shutdown (lines 827-840); pidfile stores pid+state+process start time, --stop refuses to signal a PID that fails identity (lines 682-723), and the pidfile is removed on exit (lines 870-875). Restart finalizes leftover WORKING/SUBMITTED as FAILED runner_restart (lines 790-797). Matrix proof: RunnerCoreTests + A2ALifecycleTests all ok — unique terminal finalize with ordered replay, cancel+duplicate cancel = one terminal sequence, active --stop persists CANCELED during drain and cleans pidfile, restart recovery durable, cancel race reaps complete process groups.
